**Fixed**

- On 2019 LG TVs (webOS 4.5), Bonfire did not start at all. [#34]
- With "Ask who's watching on startup" off, there was no Switch Profile button and no way to switch.
- After signing out of the iOS app, the previous account's profile stayed on the sign-in screen and carried over to the next account.
- On iPad, your own profiles could appear as a linked Bonfire, and Manage Profiles asked you to open yourself first.
- The profile picture in the header was drawn zoomed in and blurry.

**Fixed**

- Security: any account could run script in an administrator's browser through the Bonfire settings page. Please update.
- Security: a PIN typed into a TV or app sign-in screen could be guessed with no limit.
- Security: someone using a profile in a browser could take over the main account behind it.
- On Android TV, Roku and other TV apps, choosing a profile and entering its PIN was refused.
- A profile limited to one TV could be missing from that TV's sign-in screen.
- Skipping Quick Connect on known TVs also removed it for other people with the same TV model.
- Signing in on a TV could occasionally fail with a server error.
- Creating a profile could fail with "The supplied value is invalid". [#33]
- The profile picker ran off the bottom of the screen on a TV. [#31]
- A profile kept its old rating after its account's rating was lowered.
- Clearing your PIN, or using the emergency disable code, could stop your password working.
- An account with a PIN could not change its Jellyfin password.
- Creating two profiles at once could go over the profile limit.
- The Signed-in devices list in the dashboard could fail to load.
- The create form showed only four libraries at a time.

**Changed**

- A profile keeps every restriction set on its account, such as remote access, schedules and bitrate.
- Profiles in another household's Bonfire need a PIN, unless their owner allows switching on the home network.
- Hidden Bonfire profiles can no longer be opened.
- Removing someone from your Bonfire changes its code, so they cannot rejoin with the old one.
- Reopening the app keeps the profile you were using. Going back to your main profile asks for its PIN.
- Manage Profiles needs your main profile open.

**Added**

- Thirty starter avatars to pick from, on by default. Turn them off in Dashboard -> Bonfire -> Avatar Library. [#32]
- Picture quality for profile pictures and avatars: Dashboard -> Bonfire -> Picture quality.
- A New code button for your Bonfire.
- A loader for the Samsung Tizen app, so Bonfire updates reach the TV without rebuilding the app. [#16]

**Fixed**

- Giving a profile a new library in Dashboard -> Users was undone the next time anyone entered that profile. Grants made there are now kept. To take a library away from a profile, edit the profile. [#30]
- Turning on "Skip Quick Connect on known devices" took Quick Connect away from apps that already have a password screen. It now applies only to Android TV, which is the one that needs it.

**Added**

- Profiles can appear on the sign-in screens of Jellyfin for Roku, Swiftfin, Findroid and Wholphin, the same as Android TV. Turn off automatic sign in on the app, or it goes straight into the last account.
- Apps that have no user list of their own can enter a profile by typing the profile's name and its PIN.

**Changed**

- The README is shorter. Library artwork, Bonfire sharing and known limitations now have their own pages under docs/.

**Added**

- Profiles can now appear on the sign-in screen of apps that never load the web client, such as Android TV, and be opened with their PIN. New settings under Dashboard -> Bonfire -> TVs & Apps, all off until you turn them on.
- On those screens a profile shows the name you gave it, not the full account name.
- An account that owns profiles can sign in with its PIN as well as its password.
- Apps can be sent straight to the password field instead of a Quick Connect code.
- "Who's watching?" on startup can be set per device instead of everywhere at once.

**Works on Jellyfin 12.0.** The same build serves 10.11 and 12.0 — there is nothing extra to install.

**Fixed**

- On Jellyfin 12.0 the Switch Profile button was missing from the header. Its default layout keeps the old header in the page but hides it, and Bonfire was adding the button there.
- In the profile form, text boxes would not take a click and dropdowns would not open — the page jumped to the top instead. Jellyfin's account menu was being left open, and its focus handling and Bonfire's fought each other.
- The Switch Profile button could appear beside the wrong icon at the wrong size, then move a second or two later. It now appears once, beside your account icon.
- Importing avatars from a folder failed on Jellyfin 12.0, and on any server where an administrator had turned legacy authorization off.
- The Bonfire section on your profile page sat against the left edge while the rest of the page was centred.
- The rename and merge buttons in the device list were unstyled, and drew as empty boxes on televisions without an emoji font.

**Changed**

- Bonfire follows your theme's accent colour on Jellyfin 12.0, which publishes that colour under a new name.

**Fixed**

- Switching to someone's main profile wiped that person's library access, and their sub-profiles' access with it. If this has happened to you, re-tick their libraries in Jellyfin's user settings after updating. [#27]
- Switching into an administrator's account quietly removed their admin rights and hid them from the login screen. [#27]
- Restricting a profile to specific devices could lock it out of every device, including the ones you picked. [#16]
- On a TV, picking a profile changed the name at the top but left you in your main account — same libraries, same Continue Watching, same Next Up. [#16]
- On a TV, moving off the first profile jumped straight to Manage Profiles and no other profile could be reached. [#16]
- On a TV the profile cards had no size and the focus outline never appeared, so nothing looked selectable. Save could also sit below the bottom of the profile form with no way to reach it on a remote. [#16]
- The profile switcher said you were signed in as your main profile even while a sub-profile was in use.
- A profile, device or Bonfire group you had just saved could silently not be there.
- Anything added while the plugin's settings page was open was undone when an administrator pressed Save.
- One computer could appear several times in the device list, and devices that sent no name all read as "Unknown Device".
- Forgetting a profile's only allowed device silently made that profile available everywhere. It is refused now, and says which profiles are in the way.
- "Try again in 15 minutes" after too many wrong PINs. It now tells you the wait it is actually enforcing, which is usually far less.
- Device "last seen" dates reset every time Jellyfin restarted, and the device list never dropped hardware nobody uses any more.
- A language could stop loading until Jellyfin was restarted, dropping everyone back to English.
- Switching profiles on a light theme flashed a black screen, and a switch that went wrong left the screen blank for four seconds.
- The profile screen re-downloaded every profile picture on every page load. Your browser keeps them now.

**Added**

- Bonfire knows when it is on a television, and makes the profile pictures, text and focus outline large enough to use from across a room.
- Rename a device, or tell Bonfire that two entries are the same machine. "Tidy up duplicates" folds together the several devices one browser makes — a profile allowed on any of them stays allowed.
- A list of everyone signed in, with the household each profile belongs to, and a way to sign one device out.
- Export and import the plugin's configuration, so there is a copy of your profiles and PINs somewhere other than one file.
- The audit log can be filtered by name and date, and downloaded.
- Polish, contributed by danis101. [#26]
- TROUBLESHOOTING.md, which answers the most common report first: Bonfire does not edit index.html by default, so a file with no plugin tags in it is a healthy install.

**Changed**

- The Switch Profile button now sits next to your account icon in the header, instead of at the end of the row.
- The interface reads correctly on light Jellyfin themes, where separators and muted text used to be invisible.
- Bonfire does far less work in the background — most noticeable on a TV, and it steps back further while something is playing.
- The "restart to finish updating" notice now names the version running and the version waiting, so you can tell whether your restart worked. [#25]

**New**

- Bonfire no longer edits Jellyfin's `index.html`. The client script is added to the page as it is served, so there is nothing to re-apply after a Jellyfin update and no file permissions to grant. Patching the file stays available as a legacy option under **Advanced → Client script**. (#17, #11, #3)
- The switcher follows your theme's accent colour instead of always drawing Jellyfin blue.
- Profile screens use the whole window on a desktop instead of one phone-width column.
- The picker shows which profile you are currently watching as.

**Fixed**

- On Android, picking a profile could bring the picker straight back, over and over, and a PIN-protected profile could drop you at the account login.
- Picking a profile showed nothing at all for the second or two it takes, so the tap read as missed. The profile you picked now shows a spinner, and the screen no longer goes black while it loads.
- Opening a profile took several seconds and could drop you back on a screen you had already left.
- Bonfire rewrote `index.html` on startup even when set never to touch it.
- The settings page reported the client script as installed whenever the plugin was loaded at all, including on servers where nothing was reaching the page.
- Add Profile was missing from the Manage Profiles screen.
- Library names were cut off to "3D Movi…" when choosing artwork.
- **Upload avatars** and **Upload a folder** were unstyled text instead of buttons.
- "PIN Protected" showed in red and "No PIN" in green — the wrong way round.
- The audit log ran the time into the address as "12:09:28 PMIP".

**Changed**

- The plugin is called **Bonfire** in the Jellyfin sidebar.
- Plugin settings are split into tabs — General, Avatars, Accounts, Activity and Advanced — instead of one page five screens tall.
- Switcher Style and Your Bonfire move out of the profile grid into their own **Settings** screen. Bonfire Grouping is now called Your Bonfire.
- Add Profile appears on Manage Profiles only. The "Who's watching?" screen is people to pick from.
- Setting a profile picture is one panel rather than six controls. The paste-a-URL box is gone: a linked picture could not be cropped, was never stored on your server, and disappeared without warning when the link died.
- Libraries and their artwork are one list, with the artwork controls behind a switch.
- Delete is no longer as prominent as Save.

**New**

- Library artwork can be set per profile. Jellyfin builds a library tile from the items inside it, so a Kids profile could see a poster from a film it cannot open; each profile can now be given its own picture for a library, or none at all. (#19)
- Administrators can set the switcher defaults for the whole server, under Dashboard → Plugins → Bonfire. Anyone who has already chosen keeps their own setting. (#14)
- Avatars can be uploaded several at a time, or a whole folder at once. Administrators with a prepared set already on the server can point at its folder and import it. (#14)
- The profile picker has a Cancel button when you opened it yourself, so you can go back to what you were watching.

**Fixed**

- Switching a profile failed with "Invalid username or password" on Jellyfin 10.11.11, and signed the master account out. (#15)
- On Samsung Tizen, picking a profile changed the avatar but left you in the original account. (#15, #16)
- On a TV, the remote could steer the Jellyfin page hidden behind the Bonfire screen. (#16)
- The TV Back button raised Samsung’s "exit application?" prompt behind the Bonfire screen. Back now steps back one screen instead. (#15)
- "Switch Profile" now appears on the Settings page, not only in the header dropdown. (#14)
- Profile pictures could be zoomed but not dragged.
- Save and Cancel are scrolled into view when a remote reaches them, so long profile forms no longer look frozen. (#15)
- Pictures now load in clients that bundle their own web client, such as Samsung Tizen.
- A missing script tag in index.html now says which of the three causes it is. (#17)

**Changed**

- The emergency disable link appears only once an administrator has set a code.
- Error messages, hints and warnings cut down throughout.

First stable release of the 1.3 line, consolidating the 1.2.x pre-releases. ■ NEW — Tag-based content filtering. Each sub-profile can block or allow content by Jellyfin tag (for example "adults", "teens", "kids"), alongside the existing parental rating limit. Tags are inherited, so tagging a series or a whole library applies to everything inside it, and enforcement happens server-side — meaning it holds on every client, including ones that cannot show the profile switcher at all. Blocked tags are additive with the master account's, and an allow-list can only narrow the master's, so a sub-profile can never see more than its parent. ■ NEW — Reorganised profile editor. Creating and editing a profile is now grouped into four titled sections: Profile (name, colour, picture), Security (PIN, LAN bypass, auto-lock), Libraries, and Content & Device Restrictions. Previously every field sat in one flat list in the order features had been added. Sections are plain blocks rather than collapsible panels so D-pad focus order on TV stays predictable, and the layout adapts to phone widths. ■ NEW — The settings page now lists master accounts with their sub-profiles nested underneath, instead of two separate tables. ■ SECURITY — Fixed a stored cross-site scripting flaw in profile avatar images and colours. Because Bonfire groups render profiles from linked households on each other's switcher screens, a crafted value could run script in another user's browser and steal their session token. Values are now validated on the server and escaped on render. ■ SECURITY — Profile PINs are now stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes rather than unsalted SHA-256, under which a 4-8 digit PIN was recoverable almost instantly from the configuration file. Existing PINs keep working and are upgraded automatically the next time they are entered. ■ SECURITY — An account with no PIN can no longer be switched into from a shared Bonfire, and the local-network PIN bypass no longer applies when stepping into another household's account. Also removed an open redirect on the profile image endpoint. ■ FIX — The dashboard's client-script warnings are now accurate. They re-check index.html on every page load rather than reporting server-startup state, a "Re-check Now" button re-runs the injection without a Jellyfin restart, and the message names the specific cause — including whether Jellyfin can write the file at all. The advisory notice can be dismissed on installs where the file is not writable without elevating. ■ FIX — Permission-fix commands are generated for the account Jellyfin actually runs as, rather than covering every possibility at once. ■ FIX — Editing a profile no longer erases device whitelist entries for devices that are switched off, and the device picker is correctly scoped to your own household. ■ FIX — A saved PIN no longer displays as "No PIN" on your own network, and profile changes appear immediately instead of requiring a page reload. ■ PERFORMANCE — Profile switching no longer rewrites the entire audit log on the request, the client script is served with revalidation so browsers pick up updates on their own, and a listener leak that made the interface progressively less responsive over a session has been fixed.

⚠️ BETA RELEASE — not a finished release; please report issues on GitHub. ▸ Settings page: master accounts and sub-profiles were listed as two separate tables, so working out which profiles belonged to which account meant reading the "Master Account" column on every row. There is now a single list of master accounts, each with its sub-profiles collapsed underneath it behind a "2 sub-profiles" toggle. PIN status and Reset PIN are available at both levels as before. Any sub-profile whose master account no longer exists — normally the residue of a partially failed deletion — is listed separately under "Unlinked sub-profiles" rather than disappearing, so it can still be found and managed. ▸ The permission-fix commands are now generated for the account Jellyfin is actually running as, and the page states which account that is. Previously they had to cover every possibility at once: on Windows, Jellyfin runs either as a service (NT AUTHORITY\NetworkService) or as the signed-in user when installed as a tray/desktop app, so the icacls command granted Modify to ALL local users in order to work in both cases. It now grants access to exactly one account — the real one — which is both less to type and a considerably narrower permission on a file inside Program Files. ▸ The same applies to the Linux and Docker chown commands, which previously assumed the service account was named "jellyfin". That is the convention but not a guarantee, and the commands silently did nothing useful when it was not. If the account cannot be determined, the page falls back to the previous broader commands, so nothing is lost on unusual setups.

New: Tag-based content filtering for sub-profiles. Each profile can now block or allow content by Jellyfin tag (e.g. 'adults', 'teens', 'kids'), matching Jellyfin's own parental-control tag feature. Tags are inherited, so tagging a series or an entire library applies to everything inside it, and enforcement is server-side so it holds on every client. Blocked tags are additive with the master account's and an allow-list can only narrow the master's, so a sub-profile can never see more than its parent. Security: fixed a stored XSS in profile avatar images and colours — these are rendered on other households' switcher screens via Bonfire groups, so a crafted value could steal another user's session token; values are now validated server-side and escaped on render. Security: profile PINs are now stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes instead of unsalted SHA-256 (a 4-8 digit PIN was trivially recoverable from the config file); existing PINs keep working and upgrade automatically on next entry. Security: an account with no PIN can no longer be switched into from a shared Bonfire, and the LAN PIN bypass no longer applies across accounts. Security: removed an open redirect on the profile image endpoint. Fix: the client-script injection now verifies the script is actually present before reporting success — previously an index.html without the expected anchors reported success while the switcher silently never loaded, and the dashboard's failure banner could never appear. Fix: index.html is now written atomically so an interrupted write cannot corrupt the Jellyfin web client. Fix: audit log entries no longer reverse order when trimmed.

Fix: Plugin now loads correctly on Jellyfin 10.11.5. The previous release was compiled against 10.11.6, which caused a loader-level assembly version mismatch (FileNotFoundException on MediaBrowser.Common/Controller/Model) on servers running 10.11.5. Compile target downgraded to 10.11.5 — the plugin remains fully compatible with 10.11.6 and later patch releases.
Release 1.1.0: Codebase cleanup, optimization, documentation updates, and developer API reference alignment.
Initial release.

versions.changelog:
This update brings together 2.0.10.0 and 2.0.11.0 from the beta channel.

If you use the Live TV allow-list behind a reverse proxy: add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings. Without that, every request through the proxy counts as coming from the proxy, and if its address is on your list, everyone gets in. The help text now says so.

Fixed: with Live TV set up on two or more providers, the guide never used your providers' XMLTV files. They were combined into one file that could not be read past the first provider, so the guide always fell back to the simpler per-channel listings and lost categories, ratings and the other details XMLTV carries. Each provider's file is now read on its own. If one provider's file is missing or broken, only that provider's channels fall back, and the others keep their full guide (found and fixed by dillardblom).

Fixed: when two providers used the same guide id for different channels, one of them got no guide, or showed the other provider's programmes. Guide ids are now matched per provider (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: when your provider's XMLTV guide came through cut off part way, building the guide never finished. Each request for the EPG URL kept one CPU core busy until Jellyfin gave up, and the guide stayed empty. A broken file now falls back to fetching the guide per channel, as it already did when the file was missing, and no programme is listed twice (by dillardblom).

Fixed: with Dispatcharr mode on, every sync worker logged in to Dispatcharr at the same time when a sync started. Dispatcharr's login limit refused most of them, and those workers fell back to the Xtream API for the first minutes. There is now one login shared by all of them, and it waits its turn like every other request (reported by dillardblom).

This update brings together 2.0.2.0 to 2.0.9.0 from the beta channel.

If you use Live TV with the Native Tuner only, open the Live TV tab after updating and turn off the new "Publish Playlists" switch. It stays on for anyone who already had Live TV enabled, so an M3U tuner or TiviMate setup keeps working, but the native tuner does not need it.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: a single unreadable value from your provider, such as an empty value where a number belongs, no longer makes content disappear. It could blank a series' title, plot and TMDB id, drop every episode of a series, or make a whole category fail to sync. Such values are now ignored or read as 0, and an item whose ID cannot be read is skipped with a warning while the rest syncs normally (reported by foXaCe).

Fixed: changing Folder Mode, or moving a category to another folder, no longer leaves every moved item in your library twice. The old copies are removed even beyond the orphan safety limit, as long as the item only moved to another category folder; anything that actually disappeared is still protected by the limit. Moved items lose their watched status, because Jellyfin sees a new folder as a new item (reported in andreadegiovine's fork).

Fixed: when orphan cleanup removes a movie or series, the NFO and poster the plugin wrote are removed with it, so the folder no longer stays behind. Files you added yourself, such as subtitles or your own NFO, are kept, and so is the folder (idea from andreadegiovine).

Fixed: with "Group movies with the same TMDB id" on, a film whose request the provider missed no longer ends up in a folder of its own. It is held back and picked up on the next sync. Films already split this way stay split; to fix them, use Delete Movies Library in the Danger Zone and sync again (reported by andreadegiovine).

New: with "Fallback to Year-Free Lookup" on, an unmatched movie is also searched with the year of the provider's release date and with its original title, which helps when the title carries the wrong year or is in another language. A search without a year is checked against the release date, so it cannot pick a remake. A match found by the year-free retry is now remembered for later syncs, for movies and series. Movies already in your library keep their folders (idea from philx17).

New: "Publish Playlists" on the Live TV tab. The M3U and Catch-up M3U URLs contain your Xtream username and password and can be reached without a Jellyfin login. They are now only served while this switch is on, and it is off when you enable Live TV from now on. The EPG URL and channel logos are not affected (proposed by dillardblom).

New: "Restrict These URLs To" limits the Live TV URLs to the addresses you list, one per line. Leave it empty for no restriction. If you use it, include 127.0.0.1 and ::1, since Jellyfin fetches channel logos itself, and behind a reverse proxy add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings first (written by dillardblom).

Fixed: a Live TV category, channel or logo address with & in it no longer shows as & or breaks (reported by TheBazeman).

Categories load their items again on Jellyfin 12 (#117).

Jellyfin 12 stops accepting the legacy `X-Emby-Token` request header. Two of the configuration page fetch sites still sent it: the Live TV category loader and the Series / VOD content loader. Both now send `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=` instead, which Jellyfin 12's `CustomAuthentication` middleware expects. The Test connection button was never affected and still works as before. Two-line header swap in `config.js`, no server-side change.

versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

Virtual stub library entries (real-looking files with a TMDb id but no media, created by some request helpers) were counted as owned and silently excluded every personal pick. They are now recognised as virtual and ignored, so your Trakt recommendations come through
- An empty "Trakt for you" is no longer sticky: a null or empty result is cached only briefly, so once the server has your picks they appear on the next open instead of being held behind a stale empty view
- A rate-limited or unreachable Trakt is retried with a backoff (honouring the server's Retry-After) instead of being re-hit on every tab load, and the same account open on two devices now shares one fetch instead of firing two
- An unlinked user no longer sees a "Trakt for you" tab that only shows a not-linked message; the tab appears once you are linked, and "Trakt trending" (which needs no login) is always available
- The plugin log now explains an empty personal result in one line (what was fetched, what survived, and why), so a token, fetch, or ownership issue is far easier to pin down
- Tested by 6779 unit tests and 369 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

## Features

- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes

- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render

- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Developer
- Settings saved before 12.0.2.0 are no longer brought forward, so update through 12.0.2.1 first when coming from an older version
- Code, pages, and docs say logo rather than series logo, since films draw their own

## Fixes
- The Profiles page loads again instead of failing on a backdrop setting that no longer exists
- Posters with a logo draw the logo selected for a film, season, or series instead of falling back to text

## Features
- Artwork Generator is Episode Poster Generator rebuilt, with the same settings and a much wider job
- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture
- Logo designs build a text logo from any name field, with letter case, a line limit, and frame-filled letters
- Frame extraction is one set of server settings instead of a copy on every design
- Frames are ranked on tone, detail, contrast, and color rather than just clearing a threshold
- Optional setting drops a subtitle that only repeats the title
- A subtitle too long to fit can shorten to its code, shrink, or trim
- Two example designs per style, each showing a genuinely different look

## Fixes
- Seasons extract from their own episodes instead of falling back to the series backdrop
- Candidate images come from different episodes instead of clustering in one
- Heavily letterboxed frames scale back up to a usable size
- Portrait text is measured against both sides, so it no longer reads small
- Brush strokes stay thick on tall posters instead of piling into a cross
- Long titles trim at a word boundary rather than mid-word
- Descenders stay inside the safe area
- Borders, rules, and shadows scale with the poster
- A static graphic keeps its proportions
- An item with no name of its own says its one line in the larger type
- Generated images carry the item's metadata language

## Developer
- The generator, the settings model, and the configuration page are rebuilt around item kinds rather than episodes
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 that Jellyfin 12.0 ships
- Designs are found by reflection, so adding one needs a class and an enum value
- Every label, option, and default is read from the settings models
- The shared generator is split into pipeline, text, and overlay
- Frame analysis is a single pass, under a megabyte per frame instead of three and a half
- Every one-time upgrade of an older configuration sits in its own file, to be deleted whole once installs have moved on
- Tests hold the documentation, the templates, and US spelling to the code

## Features
- Shadows, rules, and the Frame border now scale with the poster, so they read the same on a 4K frame as on a DVD rip instead of turning into a hairline or a slab
- Long titles that do not fit two lines fill the first line with whole words and trim only the second, at a word boundary, instead of cutting both lines mid-word

## Fixes
- Frame drew no border at all for an episode without a name, and ignored the Show Title setting
- Cutout no longer lets a two line title run into the bottom of the cutout letters
- Split center-crops the series poster into its panel instead of stretching artwork that is not 2:3
- Brush honours the Show Episode setting and keeps a wrapped title inside the area the strokes leave clear
- Timeline keeps the marker dot inside the safe area on the first and last episode
- Text blocks are reserved from the font's real ascent and descent, so descenders no longer hang past the safe area

## Developer
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 packages Jellyfin 12.0 ships, since the plugin binds to the server's copies at runtime
- Text drawing moved from the removed SKPaint text members to SKFont, wrapped in a shared TextStyle so every style measures and draws with the same objects
- Standard and Split share one text stack; Numeral, Cutout, Brush, and Frame no longer hand-build their own paints
- Cutout renders through a canvas layer instead of a full-size scratch bitmap per poster; Split and Brush dispose their gradient shaders
- Letterbox detection scans the pixel buffer directly instead of a native call per pixel
- Bitmap scaling uses explicit cubic resampling now that FilterQuality is gone

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

Professional rating system for Jellyfin. Rate media with 1-10 stars, view detailed user ratings on hover, and see rating badges on media cards. Optimized for large libraries with lazy loading.

overview: Comprehensive rating plugin with star-based UI, average ratings display, detailed user rating popups, and performance-optimized card overlays for large media libraries.

versions.changelog: A new series gives one notification instead of one per episode. New episodes of a series you already have are grouped into one notification per season, showing which episodes arrived. Clicking a request pop-up opens that request, or the media once it is available.

Rating 10 is easier to reach. The red count on the request (+) button works on Jellyfin 12. Admins get a pop-up when someone makes a request, and users get one when their request is fulfilled. New-media pop-ups show posters and episode details again on Jellyfin 12.

Admins can remove any review. Users can hide their profile. New settings to turn off reviews and the Other Users tab. Ratings under 1 now save. Duplicates: Keep both button, correct series sizes, and no more false matches on music named "Track 01". Revision History updated.

Removes the "Unknown" cards with a blank poster and a "Not on server" tag from profiles. They were ratings of media that has since been deleted from the server and was rated before the plugin started remembering titles and posters, so there was nothing to show but the stars. They are now left out of the profile grid, reviews and activity. Deleted media that the plugin remembers keeps showing with its title and poster, as before. Nothing is deleted: if the media comes back to the library, its rating shows up again.

Fixes the stars and the reviews section appearing on library pages. Opening a library such as "Movies" or "TV Shows" from its header shows it on a details page, the same layout a movie uses, so the rating widget and "User Reviews" were added there too. People rated and reviewed the library itself, and the page then said you had rated "TV Shows". Libraries and folders no longer show the widget, and the server refuses a rating for them.

Adds a "Remove ratings left on libraries" button to the plugin's settings page, under the Jellyfin rating sync options. Updating does not delete ratings people already left on a library, and with the stars gone from library pages they could no longer remove them themselves. The button shows how many there are and on which libraries, including how many have a written review, and deletes them only after you confirm. The review text goes with them. Ratings on movies and shows are not touched.

Fixes plugin updates not reaching the browser at all. After updating, the page kept running the previous version's code, so everything fixed in a release looked like it had never been released, and only a manual hard refresh brought it through. The plugin adds its script tag to the page as Jellyfin sends it, but when the browser asked whether its copy of the page was still current, Jellyfin answered "unchanged" without sending the page - so there was nothing to add the tag to, and the browser reused its stored copy, still pointing at the old version's script, which is cached for a year on purpose and so was never re-requested. The page is now always sent in full and is no longer stored by the browser, so a new version shows up on the next ordinary page load. The large script and stylesheet keep their long-term caching.

Fixes the dashboard's Plugins page showing "An error occurred while loading plugins" after updating. Cleaning up the previous version's leftover folder removed it while Jellyfin was still running and still had it listed, and every later look at the plugin catalogue tried to write into a folder that was no longer there, which failed the whole page until Jellyfin was restarted. Only Linux and Docker servers were affected - on Windows the old files stay locked, so the folder was never actually removed. The cleanup now hands the old folder to Jellyfin to remove, the same way its own uninstall does.

Ratings can now be given to one decimal place from the rating window, not just from the stars on the movie page. Moving across the big stars shows the decimal you are about to pick and clicking takes it - 5.4, not 5 - and swiping on a phone does the same, with the star you stop on filled part-way to match. Previously each big star was a separate button, so the rating window could only ever give whole numbers. A decimal picked on the movie page also arrives in the window drawn correctly instead of being rounded down.

"No reviews yet. Be the first to write one!" is now a button. It looked like a caption, so people clicked it, nothing happened, and they scrolled back up to find the stars. It carries a pencil, highlights when you point at it, and opens the rating and review window.

Fixes a review not appearing after you write it. The review was always saved - the block of reviews further down the page just never re-read itself, so it kept showing whatever was there when the page opened, and the review only turned up once you had navigated away and back. That is why writing it a second time seemed to work: the first one had taken all along. The reviews now refresh as soon as a rating or review is added, changed or removed. A review written moments ago also used to be labelled "-1 days ago" instead of "Today", because the server stamps the time from its own clock and being a fraction of a second ahead of the browser was enough to push the age below zero.

Also fixes stale plugin folders being left behind after an update, mostly on Windows, where the old copy's file stays locked until Jellyfin restarts. The previous attempt deleted the old folder's meta.json to take it out of circulation, which turns out to do the opposite: Jellyfin treats a plugin folder with no meta.json as an active plugin named after the folder and loads it anyway. The result was two copies of this plugin running at once - doubled up services and duplicate endpoints, with the old copy able to answer requests - and a folder this plugin could no longer recognise in order to clean up. An old folder that cannot be deleted is now marked as deleted in its own manifest instead, which is what Jellyfin does itself: it is not loaded, and Jellyfin removes the folder at a later restart. Folders already left in the broken state are picked up and finished off.

Fixes the admin Ratings dashboard on Jellyfin 12, where every panel read "Failed to load" and the counters stayed empty. The dashboard's own pages were still identifying themselves the older way that Jellyfin 12 no longer accepts; they now use the current form, which Jellyfin 10.x accepts just as well, so one build covers both. The version shown at the top of the dashboard is now read from the plugin that is actually running instead of being typed into the page, so it can no longer drift out of date. The phone header also had a pass. Opening the plugin menu now keeps every button on a single line all the way down to a narrow phone, on a panel that spans the screen with even margins and rounded ends instead of sitting flush against one edge. The menu button and the account picture next to it were brought down to the size of everything else in the row, and while the menu is open the heading and the row-scrolling arrows underneath step out of sight so nothing shows through it. Closing it puts them straight back. The plugin's dialogs - media management, duplicates and the full ratings list - now fit inside a phone screen instead of pushing the page sideways.

A rebuilt rating system with real precision. Until now every rating was one of ten fixed steps, so a film was a 7 or an 8 with nothing in between. The whole star row is now a single sliding control: move across it and the stars fill smoothly under your pointer, a tenth of a star at a time, with the exact value appearing beside them as you go. Give something a 7.5 when 7 feels harsh and 8 feels generous. On a phone, swipe along the stars for the same control. The value appears while you are choosing and steps out of the way once you are done, so nothing clutters the page, and a deliberate press is still what saves a rating - simply passing over the stars never changes one you have already given. Everything you have rated before carries over untouched, and whole numbers work exactly as they always did.

Brings the header buttons back on Jellyfin 12. Jellyfin 12 rebuilt its web interface, and while it still leaves the old header in the page it collapses it to nothing - so the buttons were being created into something invisible. They now go into the new header, in the same place as before: immediately left of Jellyfin's own cast and search icons. The collapsed menu on phones is unchanged, and the buttons now also survive moving around the app, including in and out of the admin dashboard, which previously lost them until a manual refresh. Nothing changes on Jellyfin 10.x, where the old header is still used.

Fixes the plugin on Jellyfin 12, where every panel read "Failed to load" and film pages showed "Error loading ratings" (issue #83). Jellyfin 12 switched off the older ways of proving who you are and the plugin was still using them, so the server refused each request even though you were signed in - while the public files it serves kept working, which is why the interface still appeared but had no data in it. It now asks the way Jellyfin 12 expects; older Jellyfin versions accept the same form, so this one build works on both and there is nothing to choose when installing. Also stops the activity feed, top rated list and browse-by-rating from naming titles that live in libraries an account is not allowed to open.

Fixes the friends list showing "Failed to load friends" for anyone who actually had friends (issue #79). The list was loading correctly - it crashed while drawing the first friend, and that crash was being reported as a loading failure. A user with no friends never hit it, which is why it took a report to find. The panel now explains what went wrong instead of showing one generic line, offers a Retry, and is translated in every language. In media management you can also choose which copy of a duplicate to keep (issue #80) - press Keep this on any copy and the bin moves to the others, which matters when identical copies sit on different drives.

Finishes the translation work and adds a security pass. An audit of the whole plugin found another 141 phrases written straight into the markup - the profile settings window, the rating box, review comments, the media picker and its sort menu, friend menus, chat controls, moderator and ban dialogs, and every "nothing here yet" message. All of them are translated now, in all fifteen languages, and each pack carries around 560 phrases where it had about 348. On security: no exploitable weakness was found, and three things were tightened. Profile header uploads now check the file really is a GIF, MP4 or WEBM rather than trusting its name, since the address serving them is public by design. Bug report screenshots are fetched with your access token in a header instead of the web address, keeping it out of browser history. And asking for better quality now respects each account's library access. The dashboard heading also shows the right version again.

The profile page, the friends panel and the star rating widget are translated at last. Those three areas were never connected to the translation system - the words were written straight into the markup - so they stayed in English no matter which language you picked, in all sixteen languages. Forty-seven labels now go through the translation layer and are filled in for every language: the friends panel and its tabs, the profile tab strip and stat row, follow, block and friend buttons, the rating popup, and the whole sidebar down to Stats, Films, Shows, Hours, Taste, Similar Taste, Add a film, Back, Member since and the "not on server" badge. The thirty-eight strings from the quality-request and bug-report queues are translated too. Every language pack gains eighty-five entries. Thanks to chosqui for reporting it in discussion #76 with a Spanish patch that showed exactly what was missing.

Three fixes to the support queues added last release, all found by using them on a real server. The Quality and Bug Reports tabs never appeared in the Request Media window: that window is built in more than one place in the client and only one of them had been given the new tabs, so the two queues had no way in. Opening a request or a report drew the detail window underneath the one it was launched from, which made clicking a Quality row look as though nothing happened at all. And people who sent a bug report had no way of telling whether anyone had looked at it - the report box now lists your own reports beneath it with their status and any reply, and sending one no longer closes the window, so the report lands in that list in front of you. Note: after updating, reload the page with the cache cleared. The browser holds on to the page that references the previous version of the plugin's script, and until it lets go you will still be running the old one.

Two new ways for people to tell you something is wrong, and one place to work through both. A Better Quality tab on the profile searches what is already on the server, and every result carries a button to say what is wrong with the current copy - blurry, wrong audio, missing subtitles. A Report a problem button next to Edit Profile takes a description plus screenshots, pasted straight from the clipboard or picked from disk. Both land in the Request Media window as their own tabs, badged with how many are still open, where you can read the report, look at the screenshots, reply to the person who sent it, and mark it solved or declined - your reply is shown back to them. This release also fixes a profile showing 0 films and 0 hours next to a taste chart reporting hundreds of hours: those figures came from ratings alone, so anyone who watches without rating saw zeros. They now count what you have watched as well as what you have rated. And the genre breakdown was the one part of a profile with no privacy check, so a private profile's viewing habits could be read by anyone signed in.

The request list in the admin panel now lays out properly on a phone. Each request kept its title, user, date and status on a single row, so on a narrow screen the title was squeezed down to a few characters, and the media-link and rejection-reason boxes were split across a width that could not hold them. The title now takes a line of its own with the details underneath it, the expand arrow sits at the right edge, and the two input boxes stack at full width. Reported and written by @daki456. The input rules also apply in every language now - they previously keyed off the English placeholder text, so they did nothing on a translated server.

Fixes the request list in the admin panel. A category holding more requests than fit on screen squashed its cards down into unreadable slivers instead of scrolling - the cards were being compressed to fit the available height rather than keeping their own. Each category now scrolls once it passes 500 pixels, with the cards at their normal size. Thanks to @daki456 for reporting and fixing it.

Leftover trickplay cleanup now covers both ways Jellyfin stores it. Libraries set to 'save trickplay images next to media' keep the tiles in a folder beside each video rather than in the central directory, and those were invisible to the previous scan - a server using that setting appeared to have no trickplay at all. Both places are now scanned and cleaned, and the panel reports what it found in each. Verified on a live library: it correctly identified real leftovers from deleted media while leaving every folder whose video is still present untouched.

Fixes the leftover-trickplay cleanup, which previously reported nothing to clean up on every server. Jellyfin stores trickplay in folders grouped by the first two characters of each item id, and the scan was treating one of those groups as the whole directory - so it looked at a single group out of 256, usually an empty one. It now reads the real directory and looks inside every group. The panel also showed internal labels instead of readable text, and now names the directory it checked and how many folders it examined, so 'nothing to clean up' can be told apart from a scan that never ran.

Two clean-ups from the security review. Searching and browsing through the plugin now respects the libraries each account is allowed to see, so a user with limited access can no longer come across titles from libraries they cannot open - this affected the plugin's own search, the sorted library view and the latest-media list. Playback was never affected. And when the plugin refuses an action because you are not an administrator, it now says so properly instead of returning a server error; access was already correctly denied, but the message was wrong. Privacy defaults are unchanged - profiles remain visible to everyone unless the user chooses otherwise.

Security and features. Fixes three ways a user could have got script to run inside someone else's session: one through a profile's favourite films, which affected anyone viewing that profile, and two through links attached to media and deletion requests, which ran in an administrator's session. Also closes several privacy and permission gaps - private profiles could be read through the newer profile endpoints, a private list could be read by copying it, direct messages ignored blocking, the recent-requests list showed every user's requests to non-administrators, and a user banned from playback or over quota could bypass both by sending their login token in a different but equally valid form. New: leftover trickplay data can now be cleared from Media Management, so space used by tiles belonging to deleted media can be recovered without reprocessing everything you still have. Search now ignores punctuation and spacing, so 'xfiles', 'x files' and 'X-Files' all find the same show. Ratings can be edited or removed from the Ratings tab, including titles not on the server; reviews can be written for those titles; custom profile rows can be reordered; and any rating can be agreed or disagreed with, not only ones with a written review. The Reviews tab now shows posters. Fixes the empty gap under the header on phones, the plugin's buttons covering the video player in portrait, and missing posters in Recent Activity. Every endpoint now identifies you the same way, so apps signing in with a plain token are no longer refused.

Profile favourites and Media Management fixes. Adding a title from the catalog to a favourites row now works and stays: the button no longer ignores films whose name contains an apostrophe, the card is no longer discarded when you reopen the profile, and rows containing only catalog titles now show them straight away instead of only after adding something else. Titles lost by the earlier fault need re-adding once. Media Management was showing no posters, no media type and dashes for rating, plays, size and status - it now reads every field correctly, and the same fault is fixed on the Scheduled tab, the 'Leaving in' badges, and the media request and ban screens. Media that Jellyfin has not identified, which has no artwork at all, now falls back to a poster from TMDB where one can be found. On phones the header menu is now a compact row of icons rather than one full-width row per button, which previously left most buttons unreachable, plus a layout fix for the ElegantFin skin that is applied only on servers actually using it.

Fixes rating a film that is not on the server failing with a not-authenticated error. Four endpoints checked the signed-in user in a stricter way than the rest of the plugin and rejected perfectly valid requests - rating a TMDB title, reading your own rating for an item, the batch rating lookup used to draw badges, and listing or creating media requests. They now identify you the same way every other endpoint does, so any client sending a valid token is accepted.

Fixes new media being announced but never appearing in the Latest Media list. The list was ordered by the date Jellyfin takes from the file itself, not by when the media actually reached your server - so anything copied in keeping its original timestamps sorted to wherever that old date fell, usually past the end of the list. You would get the 'now available' notification and then find nothing there. The list now also includes everything the plugin announced, dated by when it actually saw it, so the notification and the list can no longer disagree. Items removed from the server since being announced are left out.

Further hardening of the watching hover card, following up the security fix in the previous version. The card no longer reads any text back out of the page at all - the title it shows while loading now comes from data the plugin already holds. Re-inserting text taken from the page undoes whatever escaping made it safe, so the read was removed rather than escaped. Numbers shown on the card (year, running time, score) are also validated as numbers before being displayed, which additionally stops an unexpected value breaking the card.

Security fix. The hover card that shows what someone is watching built an image tag by pasting an item id straight into HTML, and that id was read back out of the page. A crafted value could have escaped the image tag and run script for another user viewing the profile. Item ids are now rejected unless they are genuine Jellyfin ids, and the image is created as a real element instead of being assembled from text, so nothing untrusted can reach the markup. Reported by GitHub CodeQL (js/xss-through-dom, high severity).

API fixes for third-party and TV clients. Social endpoints previously accepted only the raw X-Emby-Token header, so any app using Jellyfin's standard authentication got 401 from every social call while the identical request worked against the ratings API - they now accept every form Jellyfin does, including API keys. All responses are also camelCase now; some endpoints returned PascalCase and others camelCase, which silently produced empty fields in other clients. Your existing data is unaffected. New endpoints make a profile page far cheaper to build: one aggregated profile call instead of nine, ratings/reviews/activity that already include title, poster and year, a per-user rating histogram, a capability check, and paging on followers and following. Nothing changes in the web interface.

Hover what someone is watching to see the poster and details. Pointing at the title in the Similar Taste list now brings up a card with the artwork, year, running time, age rating, community score, genres and a synopsis - so you can tell what it is without leaving the profile. For an episode it shows the series artwork and the episode name. Details are fetched once and remembered for the rest of the session.

Live presence, full titles, and a Watch too button. The Similar Taste list now updates by itself when someone comes online or starts watching - you no longer have to close and reopen the profile to see it. What someone is watching moved onto its own line, so long series titles are readable in full instead of being squeezed between the name and the match percentage. And each person who is watching now has a Watch too button: press it and you are asked whether to join them at the point they are at right now, or start from the beginning.

See who is online and what they are watching, and a much better looking profile name. The Similar Taste list now shows a dot on each person: bright green and pulsing means they are watching something right now, and the card shows what it is with a clock that ticks along live; soft green means online but not watching; grey means offline. The profile name has also been fixed - it was drawn as a colour gradient clipped to the letters, which over a photo or video header turned it into washed-out grey. It is now solid white with proper display typography, using each platform's large-text typeface.

See what you actually watch, find people with the same taste, and Back now works properly. Profiles have a new Taste ring in the sidebar showing your genre breakdown by real watch time - taken from what you have actually played, not just what you rated - with total hours and a percentage per genre. Below it, a Similar Taste list ranks everyone on the server by how closely their genre mix matches yours, showing the genres you have most in common; click anyone to open their profile, or use the envelope button to message them directly. Also fixed: opening someone's profile from a followers or match list and pressing Back used to close the whole profile window instead of returning to the profile you came from.

Rate films that are not on the server, keep ratings readable after media is deleted, choose your TMDB search language, and browse other users. You can now rate a title added to a profile row from the catalog even though it is not on the server - hover it and press Rate. If it is added to the library later, your rating attaches to it automatically. Ratings also remember the title, year and poster of what you rated, so deleting a film no longer leaves a nameless row of stars behind; older ratings fill this in as you use them. Admins can set the language TMDB search returns titles in (Settings, TMDB Search Language) instead of always getting English. And profiles have a new Other Users tab listing everyone on the server, with a filter box, so you can find and visit other people's profiles without knowing their name in advance.

Header buttons now fold into a dropdown menu on phones. With search, language, profile, requests, notifications, latest media, chat and friends all in the header there was simply not enough room on a small screen, and buttons ended up clipped or wrapping badly. On phone-sized screens they now sit behind a single arrow button and open as a tidy list, with the search box at full width. Unread chat messages light a dot on that button so you can still tell something is waiting inside. Nothing changes on tablets or desktop. Thanks to @chosqui for the suggestion (discussion #71).

Fixes from reported issues. The Save button in Profile Settings now works - it was calling an address the server does not accept, so nothing was ever saved, and the privacy tick-boxes always looked switched on regardless of your real settings (#72). The search bar no longer disappears on phones held in portrait: it shrinks to just the magnifier icon and expands when tapped, instead of being hidden on any screen under 400px wide (#69). Deleting media now also removes its trickplay thumbnails and any extracted subtitles or attachments, which used to be left behind forever (#70). Uninstalling the plugin now really removes the header buttons - the plugin no longer edits Jellyfin's index.html, and it cleans up that edit if an older version made one, so users no longer have to clear their browser cache by hand (#66). When an old plugin folder cannot be deleted on Windows because its file is locked, the plugin now removes that folder's meta.json so the stale version stops being listed and loaded (#67). New-media notifications now log why an item was treated as new, to make the remaining reports diagnosable (#65).

Much smaller downloads and far less disk activity. The plugin's script, stylesheet and language files are now sent pre-compressed, so a first page load transfers roughly 108 KB instead of 676 KB - about six times less. This applies even if you reach Jellyfin over HTTPS directly, where Jellyfin's own compression is off by default. Separately, rapid saves are now merged into a single write: previously every user's presence heartbeat rewrote the entire online-users file, so a few people online meant constant disk churn. Nothing is lost - pending saves are flushed on shutdown and before any backup export or import.

Big speed and smoothness pass. Pages load about a third lighter: the plugin's styles are now a proper stylesheet instead of being stuffed inside the script, and only your own language is downloaded rather than all sixteen. Scrolling through libraries is noticeably smoother because the plugin no longer re-scans the whole page every time anything on it changes. The admin Media list now asks the database for just the page you're looking at instead of loading your entire library first, so it opens quickly even on large collections. Chat only fetches new messages instead of re-downloading the last 50 every two seconds, and background tabs stop polling entirely. Watching something no longer rewrites a settings file every few seconds of playback. Data files are also written more safely, so a crash or power cut mid-save can no longer leave them corrupted. Includes the admin category list scrollbar fix from PR #73.

Properly fixes the 'new media' pop-ups that kept appearing for films and shows already on your server. The plugin now learns your whole existing library the first time it runs and only alerts you about genuinely new additions. A library scan, a re-scan, or installing the plugin on a big existing collection no longer floods you with 'now available' alerts for old content - including whole seasons that were already there. Re-scans and re-added files no longer fool it either.

Your ratings now live in Jellyfin too, plus a compatibility fix. Every rating you give is also saved into Jellyfin's own rating, so other apps and tools (like Maintainerr) can find and use your ratings. A one-time 'Sync existing ratings to Jellyfin' button in the plugin settings copies all your past ratings across in one click; new ratings are saved automatically. There's also an optional setting to write the average score into each item's Community Rating (off by default - it replaces the existing IMDb/TMDB score and is undone when Jellyfin refreshes metadata). Fix: the Friends panel (Online tab, friend search) and live chat no longer throw errors on the latest Jellyfin (10.11.10/10.11.11).

Fixes: deleting a duplicate now really removes the file (no more reappearing), the rating number no longer sticks after you move off a star, header text stays readable over a video background, and dragging from Recent Activity now reliably sticks.

Speed and reliability improvements. Made the 'Latest Media' panel and general browsing noticeably faster on large libraries by removing heavy background work that ran every minute. Fixed old movies and shows sometimes appearing as 'newly added' when they were not - now only genuinely new media triggers a notification, and the same item is never announced twice (even after a server restart). Fixed custom sorting showing no cards when several folders are combined into one library view.

Faster loading and a duplicate-finder fix. Pages now open quicker: the plugin's add-on is cached by your browser and packaged about a third smaller, so it doesn't re-download every time.
